PWR5.note: Main 5 V input, 4.75–5.25 V. Connect all six +5V pins.

PWR33.note: 3.3 V output of the CM4 regulator: 300 mA per pin, 600 mA total. Feeds GPIO_VREF and the status LEDs; heavy loads take their own regulator.

SD.note: eMMC variant: SD interface is not brought out. Leave unconnected.

ANALOG.note: No USB-C PD on this board: leave unconnected.

3.note: To the Ethernet switch port (PHY-to-PHY link: transformer or capacitive coupling, schematic engineer's choice). 100 Ω pair.

5.note: To the Ethernet switch port. 100 Ω pair.

4.note: To the Ethernet switch port. 100 Ω pair.

6.note: To the Ethernet switch port. 100 Ω pair.

9.note: To the Ethernet switch port. 100 Ω pair.

11.note: To the Ethernet switch port. 100 Ω pair.

10.note: To the Ethernet switch port. 100 Ω pair.

12.note: To the Ethernet switch port. 100 Ω pair.

15.note: Link activity LED, active low, 8 mA sink.

17.note: Speed LED (low = 1 Gbit or 100 Mbit link), active low, 8 mA sink.

19.note: Speed LED (low = 1 Gbit or 10 Mbit link), active low, 8 mA sink.

20.note: Jumper to GND write-protects the bootloader EEPROM; otherwise leave floating (100 kΩ internal pull-up).

21.note: Activity LED: active low, 20 mA max, 5 V tolerant.

36.note: To GPS RX (Beitian BK-450; later an LTE modem with GPS). At boot the firmware probes GPIO0/1 as I2C0 for a HAT EEPROM — a few pulses reach the GPS RX; disable the probe with force_eeprom_read=0 (see Layout notes). Overlay: dtoverlay=uart2.

58.note: Sensor bus: ADS1115 (4× RSSI), INA228 / Matek INA-BM, RM3100, BMP390, BK-450 compass, receiver-module ID EEPROM. 1.8 kΩ pull-up already on the CM4 — do not add strong external pull-ups.

56.note: I2C1 clock. 1.8 kΩ pull-up on the CM4.

54.note: To CRSF TX1 (TBS Crossfire). Single-wire half-duplex: direction buffer + inverter on the baseboard. Overlay: dtoverlay=uart3 plus a custom overlay that muxes only GPIO7 to RTS3 (the stock uart3,ctsrts would also take GPIO6 as CTS3).

37.note: Half-duplex direction for TX1. As RTS3 the kernel PL011 RS-485 mode (Linux ≥ 5.13) asserts it for the duration of each transmission; polarity via rs485-rts-active-low in DT or TIOCSRS485. Usable as a plain GPIO instead.

30.note: CVBS 4→1 switch select, bit 0. Pull-up at boot (= 1, channel 1). This pin is CTS3: the stock uart3,ctsrts overlay would claim it — use an RTS-only overlay.

39.note: To CRSF TX2 (ExpressLRS). Single-wire half-duplex: direction buffer + inverter on the baseboard. Overlay: dtoverlay=uart4 plus an RTS-only overlay for GPIO11.

44.note: CVBS 4→1 switch select, bit 1. Pull-down at boot. This pin is CTS4: the stock uart4,ctsrts overlay would claim it — use an RTS-only overlay.

38.note: Half-duplex direction for TX2 — same scheme as CRSF1_DIR (RTS4 in RS-485 mode, or plain GPIO).

31.note: To the ST3025 servo bus (2 servos, 1 Mbit/s, single wire). Automatic direction on the baseboard (TX-driven buffer as inside the Waveshare Bus Servo Adapter (A)); no direction GPIO. Overlay: dtoverlay=uart5.

55.note: Service console on a 3-pin header (GND, TXD, RXD), 3.3 V. The only UART the bootloader writes to (BOOT_UART=1); default kernel console (console=serial0). Field recovery without a monitor.

29.note: Signal inversion select for TX2 (XOR or mux on the baseboard). Pull-down at boot.

50.note: Power switch enable for CRSF TX1 (12 V, up to 2 W RF). Pull-down at boot keeps the module off until software enables it; add a pull-down at the switch gate too.

49.note: Fan PWM, hardware PWM0 channel 0 (dtoverlay=pwm,pin=18,func=2). Low at boot: if the fan must run before software starts, add a pull-up at the driver input.

26.note: Power switch enable for CRSF TX2. Pull-down at boot = off.

27.note: Shared DATA line of the four receivers (RTC6705-type, 25-bit write-only words). Hardware SPI6: dtoverlay=spi6-1cs,cs0_pin=22 (the default CS0 = GPIO18 is FAN_PWM) — or bit-bang.

25.note: Shared CLK line of the four receivers.

46.note: LE of receiver 1: low while shifting, latched on the rising edge (= active-low chip select). Pull-down at boot.

24.note: Fan tachometer input. Open-collector output — add a pull-up on the baseboard; the internal 47 kΩ is too weak for a long cable.

48.note: Signal inversion select for TX1 (XOR or mux on the baseboard). Pull-down at boot.

78.note: GPIO_VREF: tie to CM4_3.3V (pins 84/86) for 3.3 V GPIO. Must not float or be grounded — the CM4 will not start.

80.note: Camera/decoder I2C0 clock (BCM GPIO45): to the CSI0 camera FFC and to the ADV7280A-M on CSI1. 1.8 kΩ pull-up on the CM4.

82.note: Camera/decoder I2C0 data (BCM GPIO44). Clients: CSI0 camera module, ADV7280A-M at 0x21 (ALSB high) or 0x20 (ALSB low). 1.8 kΩ pull-up on the CM4.

89.note: Jumper to GND disables Wi-Fi (ELRS 2.4 GHz module nearby). 1.8 kΩ pull-up on the CM4; as an input it reports the module state.

91.note: Jumper to GND disables Bluetooth. 1.8 kΩ pull-up on the CM4.

92.note: Reset button: to GND through 220 Ω. As an output: high = power good and CPU running (drive a LED through a buffer). 10 kΩ internal pull-up to 3.3 V.

93.note: Jumper or button to GND forces USB boot (rpiboot: eMMC flashing, recovery). Must be low within 2 ms of +5V rising. 10 kΩ internal pull-up.

95.note: Power LED, active low, must be buffered (transistor) per datasheet.

97.note: To the CSI0 camera FFC (camera enable / shutdown). Do not reassign.

99.note: From the Ethernet-reboot circuit (independent of the CM4), open-drain only. Low = CM4 fully off (15 µA), 3.3 V and 1.8 V outputs drop; release = cold start. 100 kΩ internal pull-up to +5V with RC delay.

100.note: Output: low during reset, high (3.3 V) once the CPU has started. Can reset peripherals such as the USB hub.

101.note: Tie to GND for fixed host role (needs the OS driver). rpiboot needs a direct USB path CM4 ↔ PC in device mode: a switch or jumper between the hub upstream and the service port (schematic engineer's choice).

103.note: USB 2.0 D−, 90 Ω pair, intra-pair match 0.15 mm. To the USB 2.0 hub upstream (2 external ports, LTE modem, spare) / rpiboot service port. OS: otg_mode=1.

102.note: To M.2 CLKREQ#. Mandatory: without it the CM4 does not output REFCLK. Internal pull-up.

109.note: To M.2 PERST#. Mandatory for a clean SSD reset.

110.note: To M.2 REFCLK+, 100 MHz, 90 Ω pair, intra-pair match 0.1 mm. AC-coupling capacitor already on the CM4.

116.note: From M.2 PERp0 (SSD transmitter). 90 Ω pair. AC-coupling capacitors are on the SSD side (present on NVMe cards).

122.note: To M.2 PETp0. 90 Ω pair. AC-coupling capacitor already on the CM4.

128.note: To the camera FFC (CSI0, 2 lanes), 100 Ω pair. CM4IO uses a 22-pin 0.5 mm FFC; Raspberry Pi cameras use 15-pin 1.0 mm (adapter cable).

130.note: To the camera FFC, 100 Ω pair.

134.note: To the camera FFC, 100 Ω pair.

136.note: To the camera FFC, 100 Ω pair.

140.note: To the camera FFC, 100 Ω pair. Software: the stock cam0 overlay variants expect the camera I2C on GPIO0/1; here I2C0 is on pins 82/80, so the overlay must reference i2c_csi_dsi (one-line change).

142.note: To the camera FFC, 100 Ω pair.

115.note: From ADV7280A-M D0N (pin 10), 100 Ω pair. Single-lane CSI-2 link. Overlay: dtoverlay=adv728x-m,adv7280m=1 (targets CSI1 and I2C0 on pins 82/80 by default).
